prompt:

Preserve the silhouette, vent layout, visor shape, dark finish and straps from the photograph. The small existing light-colored wordmark stays subtle and unchanged; never invent lettering. It is a vented BICYCLE helmet, with NO transparent face shield, no motorcycle ear covers, no LED, no camera and no extra accessory. Do not invent safety certification, impact-test performance, weight, material grade, sizing or price.
One fictional Vietnamese adult woman, about 28 years old, oval face, medium-length dark hair tied in a low ponytail, olive-green zip cycling jacket, plain black athletic trousers, short natural nails, no jewelry. Friendly understated expression, no resemblance to a named real person. Keep the exact same face, ponytail and clothing across scenes. Her mouth stays relaxed, no talking or lip-sync; male Vietnamese voice-over will be added separately.
If a second reference is supplied, use it for the exact fictional presenter's identity and clothes, not as a replacement helmet design. The helmet is the main subject, no oversized proportions, no duplicate helmet. Plausible hands, five fingers per hand, no extra limbs. Keep all important helmet parts within the central 80% of the frame. No graphic overlays, subtitles, captions, price cards or watermark.
On the SAME leafy park cycle path, wider three-quarter-length shot of the SAME presenter wearing the same exact helmet correctly with secured chin strap, olive jacket and black athletic trousers. She stands beside a stationary simple matte dark bicycle, one hand lightly on handlebar, both feet on ground. She is NOT seated or riding. Lush green background, natural daylight. Helmet remains large enough to identify, no other people or helmets.
